preconditions.title: Org administrator authenticated on the staging API with generate-text deployed
preconditions.definition:
1. The staging API runs a build that contains DK26-3159 (generate-text) and DK26-3221 (Create an Assessment from File).
2. An organisation administrator who can manage tests is signed in, and their access token and organizationId are available to an API client such as Postman.
3. The API contract 'Create an Assessment from File: API Contract (DK26-3221 / DK26-3220)', revision 4, section 3a, is open for reference. The request is POST /assessment-import/:organizationId/:importId/tests/:sheet/generate-text with the body { field, title, difficultyLevel }.

preconditions.title: A prepared workbook has been uploaded and its import is less than 24 hours old
Users and organisations for permission and isolation checks
preconditions.definition:
1. User B belongs to the same organisation but their role cannot manage tests, and their access token is available.
2. An administrator of a different organisation is available, with their own organizationId and an importId from their own upload.
3. Both tokens can be used in the API client.

preconditions.title: Developer support to produce the expired, limit and AI failure states
preconditions.definition:
1. An import that was checked more than 24 hours ago is available, or the developer can expire one on staging.
2. The developer (Fuad Muhammed) can make the AI usage budget run out on staging, for example by lowering it temporarily.
3. The developer can make the AI service fail or time out on staging, for example with a bad key or a test switch.
4. These settings are put back to normal after the test.

tests.title: A test description is generated for a test in an uploaded file
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; a prepared workbook uploaded less than 24 hours ago, with its importId and sheet names recorded.
steps: Send generate-text for one sheet with the body { "field": "description", "title": <the sheet's test title>, "difficultyLevel": <its difficulty> }.
Read the status code and the response body.
Check the data.sheet, data.field and data.text values.
Read the text and compare it with the sheet's questions and categories.
tests.expected: The request returns 200 with success true, data.sheet equal to the sheet name, data.field 'description' and data.text set. The text is plain text (no HTML or Markdown headings), no more than 250 characters, and describes what this test covers.

tests.title: Test instructions are generated for a test in an uploaded file
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; a prepared workbook uploaded less than 24 hours ago.
steps: Send generate-text for one sheet with field 'instructions', the sheet's title and its difficulty.
Read the status code and the response body.
Check the format of any list in the text.
Read the text as a candidate would.
tests.expected: The request returns 200 with data.field 'instructions' and plain text of at most 250 characters. Any list is one '- ' line per item, as the contract describes. The text reads as guidance for a candidate taking this test.

tests.title: Generated text is based on that test's own title, difficulty, categories and questions
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; the uploaded workbook has two sheets on clearly different topics.
steps: Generate a description for the first topic's sheet and then for the second topic's sheet.
Compare each text with its own sheet's questions and categories.
Generate a description for the first sheet again, this time sending a different title and difficulty in the body than in the file (as unsaved Edit Test panel values).
Compare the new text with the previous one.
tests.expected: Each text matches its own sheet's subject and categories, and neither mentions the other sheet's topic. When a different title and difficulty are sent, the text follows the values in the request, not the file, so it matches what the user sees in the panel.

tests.title: Generated instructions never state the number of questions, time limit or pass mark
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; a prepared workbook uploaded, including the sheet with more than 40 questions.
steps: Generate instructions at least 10 times across different sheets, including the sheet with more than 40 questions.
In each text, look for any count of questions (for example '20 questions'), any duration (minutes, hours, 'time limit') and any pass mark or percentage.
Generate descriptions 5 times and check them the same way.
tests.expected: None of the generated instructions states the number of questions, a time limit or duration, or a pass mark or percentage, because these can still change before the assessment is created. If a description includes any of these, record it as a risk for the write-up, even though the acceptance criterion names only instructions.

tests.title: Generated text always stays within 250 characters
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; a prepared workbook uploaded, including the sheet with more than 40 questions.
steps: Generate a description and instructions for every sheet, at least 20 calls in total.
Send some calls with a title of the full 255 characters.
Measure the length of each data.text, counting every character including newlines and '- ' list markers.
Check whether any text ends mid-word or mid-sentence.
tests.expected: Every text is 250 characters or fewer, including for long titles and the largest sheet. Text is not cut off mid-word or mid-sentence to fit the limit; if any is, it is recorded as a finding.

tests.title: Generated text never reveals the answers to the test's questions
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; the uploaded workbook has a sheet whose correct answers are distinctive words that do not appear in the questions.
steps: For the sheet with distinctive answers, generate a description 5 times and instructions 5 times.
Search every text for each distinctive answer word and for any phrasing that gives away a correct option.
Repeat for one ordinary sheet, comparing its texts with its answer column.
tests.expected: No generated text contains a correct answer, an answer option marked as correct, or a hint that points to one. The contract says answers are never sent to the AI, so a distinctive answer word appearing would show that they are being sent.

tests.title: Question text that tries to instruct the AI does not change what it does
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; the uploaded workbook has a sheet with a question that tries to instruct the AI.
steps: Generate a description and instructions for that sheet, 3 times each.
Check whether any text follows the embedded instruction, for example by listing answers, changing language or tone, adding links, or leaving the task.
Check that every text is still a short description or set of instructions for the test, within 250 characters.
tests.expected: The AI ignores instructions written inside question text. Every text is still an ordinary description or set of instructions within 250 characters, with no answers, links, scripts or other off-task content.

tests.title: Generating text saves nothing, and each call gives a new version
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; a prepared workbook uploaded less than 24 hours ago.
steps: Request GET /assessment-import/:organizationId/:importId and save the response.
Send generate-text for the same sheet and field 3 times, keeping each text.
Request the import again and compare it with the saved response.
Check the domain's tests list and the Tests list for anything new.
tests.expected: Each call returns a different version of the text. The import's tests, descriptions, instructions and status are unchanged after generating, and no test, question or assessment has been created. Nothing is stored until the assessment is created.

tests.title: Generated text is kept only when it is sent with Create
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; a prepared workbook uploaded less than 24 hours ago; a domain to create into is chosen.
steps: Generate a description and instructions for test A, and generate a description for test B.
Send create (POST .../:importId/assessment) with test A's generated description and instructions in its tests entry, and with test B's description set to null (as if the user discarded it).
Open the created tests A and B.
Compare their description and instructions with what was generated and what was sent.
tests.expected: Test A is created with exactly the text sent in the create request. Test B has no description, even though one was generated for it. Only what the user saved and sent with create is kept.

tests.title: Invalid generate requests are refused with field-level errors
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; a prepared workbook uploaded less than 24 hours ago.
steps: Send generate-text with field set to 'summary', then with field missing.
Send it with title missing, empty, only spaces, and 256 characters long.
Send it with difficultyLevel 'Expert', then with it missing.
Read each status code and errors list.
tests.expected: Each request returns 400 with code VALIDATION_FAILED, success false and an errors list. Each problem has step 'configureTests', the field it belongs to (field, title or difficultyLevel) and a code such as REQUIRED, INVALID_VALUE or OUT_OF_RANGE. Nothing is generated and no AI usage is consumed.

tests.title: Unknown imports and sheets return 404, and encoded sheet names work
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; the uploaded workbook includes a sheet named 'Functions & Scope'.
steps: Send generate-text for the sheet 'Functions & Scope', URL-encoded as Functions%20%26%20Scope.
Send it for a sheet name that is not in the workbook.
Send it with a well-formed importId that does not exist.
Send the 'Functions & Scope' sheet name without URL encoding.
tests.expected: The encoded sheet name returns 200 and text for that sheet. An unknown sheet or importId returns 404 with code NOT_FOUND. The unencoded name either works or returns a clear 400 or 404, never a 500.

tests.title: Users who cannot manage tests are refused
tests.preconditions: User B (cannot manage tests) authenticated on staging; an importId from the same organisation is recorded.
steps: As User B, send generate-text for a sheet in the organisation's import.
Read the status code and body.
As the org administrator, request the check result for the same import and look at permissions.tests.
tests.expected: User B gets 403 with code FORBIDDEN and no generated text. The check response shows that this permission is missing for User B, so the screen can hide or disable the buttons.

tests.title: Text can only be generated for imports in the user's own organisation
tests.preconditions: Org administrators of organisations A and B authenticated; each has an importId from their own upload.
steps: As organisation A's administrator, send generate-text with organisation A's organizationId and organisation B's importId.
As organisation A's administrator, send it with organisation B's organizationId and importId.
Read each status code and body.
tests.expected: Both requests are refused (404 for an import that is not in that organisation, or 403 for the wrong organisation) and return no text. The responses reveal nothing about organisation B's import, sheets or questions, and no AI usage is consumed.

tests.title: Generating without authentication is rejected
tests.preconditions: A valid organizationId, importId and sheet name are recorded.
steps: Send generate-text with no access token.
Send it with an invalid or expired token.
Read each status code and body.
tests.expected: Both requests are rejected with 401 Unauthorized, return no generated text and consume no AI usage.

tests.title: An expired import answers 410 EXPIRED
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; an import checked more than 24 hours ago is available.
steps: Send generate-text for a sheet in the expired import.
Read the status code and errors.
Upload the same workbook again and generate text for the same sheet in the new import.
tests.expected: The expired import returns 410 with code EXPIRED, so the screen can send the user back to Upload. After uploading again, generation works for the new import.

tests.title: Usage limit and AI failure return different, clear responses
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; the developer can make the AI usage budget run out and make the AI service fail.
steps: With the developer's help, make the AI usage budget run out, then send generate-text.
Restore the budget. With the developer's help, make the AI service fail or time out, then send generate-text.
Compare the two responses: status code, code, message and step.
Restore normal settings and send generate-text once more.
tests.expected: When the limit is reached, the response is 429 with code AI_LIMIT_REACHED, meaning try again later. When the AI fails or times out, it is 503 with code AI_UNAVAILABLE, meaning try again now. Both use the standard error format with step 'configureTests' and never return partial or empty text as success. After the settings are restored, generation works again.

tests.title: Generation answers within 30 seconds and works for an import in any status
tests.preconditions: Org administrator authenticated on staging; a prepared workbook uploaded less than 24 hours ago.
steps: Time 10 generate-text calls across different sheets and fields.
Record the average and slowest response times.
Create the assessment from this import, then send generate-text for one of its sheets again.
tests.expected: Every call returns within 30 seconds, the limit in the contract. A call that would take longer ends with 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE rather than hanging. After the assessment is created, generation still works for the import, since nothing is saved, and the created tests are not changed.

tests.title: Quality findings, risks and recommendations are written up
tests.preconditions: Access to Confluence and to DK26-3159; the results of TC-03 to TC-07 and TC-17 are available.
steps: Look for the write-up on DK26-3159 or on the API contract page.
Check that it covers text quality, the risks (answer leakage, prompt injection, length, wrong figures) and recommendations for wider use, such as assessment-level instructions.
Compare its findings with what TC-03 to TC-07 and TC-17 observed.
tests.expected: A write-up is linked from DK26-3159 and covers quality findings, risks and recommendations for wider use, consistent with what testing found. As of 2026-10-28 no write-up exists, so this test fails until one is published.
